haiku-low.q1: Reads reports.row_count. At 10,000 or fewer rows it returns 200 text/csv directly. Above that it records an export, queues a job, and returns 202 JSON; the user later gets a 24-hour emailed and page link.
haiku-low.q2: It returns the existing active export with 202 and existing:true, starting no second job. The rule is per user and report, not per view, so the page says an earlier export is still running.
haiku-low.q3: The link works for 24 hours (expires_at). The bucket deletes the stored file 7 days after creation. There is no cleanup job, and the page shows link expired after expiry.
haiku-low.q4: Up to three attempts, with waits of 60 s then 300 s. After the last failure, fail_export marks it failed, shows the short error, and sends one export_failed email. The user can export again.
haiku-low.q5: Report rows are read only from the read replica, by both the rows API and the export job. The primary holds only export metadata in report_exports.
haiku-low.q6: In the report_exports table on the primary database. The page polls GET /exports/latest every 5 seconds while queued or running, and on reopening it fetches the newest export.
haiku-low.q7: It streams report_rows in 5,000-row keyset pages into one 8 MB buffer, uploading each full buffer as a multipart part and keeping only etags and a count. Runtime for 2 million rows is still unmeasured.
haiku-low.q8: Partly written data is discarded: the next attempt aborts the old upload and restarts from the first row. The object is invisible until complete_multipart, so no half-written file is downloadable.
haiku-low.q9: The POST copies filters and cols from the URL, validates them, and stores them as text on the report_exports record. The job payload carries only export_id, so the job reads them from the record.
haiku-low.q10: A unique partial index on (user_id, report_id) where status is queued or running. The insert uses ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; a request that gets no row returns the active export.
haiku-low.q11: The record must be done, with expires_at set and a signed URL made for the remaining time. On a rerun of a done export, the job only sends the email if notified_at is empty, and otherwise does nothing.
haiku-low.q12: Any error before the last row returns 500 with no file, because the CSV is sent only when complete. Nothing is stored, and the user can click again. A stale count moves it to the large path.

sonnet.q1: The endpoint reads reports.row_count. 10,000 rows or fewer: the response is the CSV itself (200, text/csv, attachment), no job, nothing stored. More than 10,000: it saves an export record, queues one background job and returns 202 with JSON (export_id, status, filters, cols, existing); the job writes the file to the exports bucket and emails a 24-hour link. (A stale count during the small path falls back to the large path.)
sonnet.q2: The click returns 202 with the existing active export and existing: true; no second job starts. This holds during retry waits. The rule is per user and report, not per view, so a click with different filters also returns the earlier export, and the page says an earlier export is still running. (An orphan record, queued with no job_id and older than 2 minutes, is re-queued instead.)
sonnet.q3: The link works 24 hours (expires_at = now + 24h; emailed and page links both end at expires_at). The bucket deletes the object 7 days after creation. There is no cleanup job; records stay as history.
sonnet.q4: 3 attempts (waits of 60 s then 300 s; each attempt killed after 1,800 s). After the last fails, on_final_failure calls fail_export: the record becomes failed with a short error, any upload is aborted, and the user gets one export_failed email (if notified_at empty). The page shows failed with the error, and the user can start a new export.
sonnet.q5: The read replica (report_rows, and reports.row_count). The primary database is used only for report_exports metadata.
sonnet.q6: In the report_exports table's status column (queued, running, done, failed) on the primary database. The page calls GET /api/reports/{report_id}/exports/latest on page load (including when the user returns later) and after a 202, and polls every 5 seconds while queued or running, stopping on done or failed.
sonnet.q7: It streams: reads the replica in keyset pages of 5,000 rows, writes CSV into one in-memory 8 MB buffer, uploads each full buffer as a multipart part (keeping etags), then uploads the final part and calls complete_multipart. Memory is just one 8 MB buffer, one page and the etag list (about 113 parts for 900 MB). Must finish within 1,800 s per attempt; throughput is unmeasured and is an open risk.
sonnet.q8: The object stays invisible until complete_multipart succeeds, so no half-written file is downloadable. If the handler can still run, it aborts the upload, sets status back to queued with the error, and re-raises. If the worker is killed, the record stays running with its old upload_id; the next attempt aborts that upload, and the bucket discards leftover uploads after 24 hours. Each retry restarts from the first row (no progress is kept).
sonnet.q9: In the export record (report_exports filters and cols columns, as validated text), saved at step 3. The job payload is only the export_id; the job loads the record and uses the same filters and columns.
sonnet.q10: The database: a unique partial index on (user_id, report_id) where status IN ('queued','running'), used with INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING *. If no row returns, the loser selects the active export and replies 202 with existing: true.
sonnet.q11: complete_multipart must have returned (or the record is already done) and the record updated to status done with expires_at set (UPDATE ... WHERE status='running'); then signed_url is made and the email sent, then notified_at set. If the queue reruns it: a record that is done with notified_at empty only sends the email (file not rebuilt); done with notified_at set returns at once and sends nothing; a failed record returns without raising. If the UPDATE matches no row, it reloads and goes on only if done.
sonnet.q12: The server returns 500 with no file (the file is sent only when complete, so a cut-off file never looks whole). Nothing is stored; the user can click again.
